subtype: Approach: analysis paralysis over an irreversible choice [Pitfall]
passage: My name is Sachin, and I did not choose my stream; the deadline did. For six weeks I read forums at night. Every answer added another option: Commerce with Maths, Humanities with Psychology, Science without Biology, a diploma, an arts college. My list on the phone grew to fourteen lines. Each choice felt like closing ten doors. Amandeep, my uncle, asked kindly, "Have you decided?" and I said, "Almost." On the last day for forms the school office put me in the default section, because a blank form goes to the default. Not what I would have picked. Not what I would have avoided either. That is the strange part: nobody made a bad choice. Nobody made one.

qa.q: How many lines did the list on Sachin's phone reach?
What was Sachin feeling about choosing?
qa.a: Afraid of closing doors, so stuck and anxious.

qa.q: What could Sachin have done to decide before the deadline?
qa.a: Set a decision date, shortlist two options and ask a counsellor, because unlimited options guarantee delay.

qa.q: How might Amandeep have felt when Sachin said "Almost"?
qa.a: Possibly worried but patient, since Amandeep asked kindly and did not press.

grounding: A student reads forums, keeps adding options and fears closing doors, so the deadline passes and someone else makes the default choice.
